items.question: A trading app's entry is an OTOCO order whose take-profit and stop legs are placed at the FULL entry amount on the first partial fill, and the take-profit leg is not reduce-only, so a partial fill followed by a TP fill can flip the account short with no stop. One contract is 10 USD and cannot partially fill. Risk sizing, awaiting a go-live decision, produces sizes of 80-90 USD. The real fix (legs that track filled quantity) needs exchange experiments first. What now?

options.label: (a)
options.text: Add a code guard: in the live environment, refuse any entry above 10 USD (manual or bridge) until the partial-fill fix ships; testnet stays uncapped for the experiments.

options.label: (b)
options.text: No code: the owner holds risk sizing's go-live and keeps the Amount box at 10 by discipline.

options.label: (c)
options.text: Do nothing until the full partial-fill fix ships.

items.rationale: (a) makes the S0 unreachable in live whatever is typed or enabled, and costs nothing at today's 10 USD. (b) relies on memory across a 6-week absence and a server migration. (c) leaves the S0 one setting away.

items.question: An audit found that every protection in an order app hangs off one stop order's state machine or a UI toggle: an emergency market-close that cancels the stop before confirming the close, no handling of a rejected stop leg, reconnect that gives up after 10 tries, position side taken from a UI toggle, and a restore that never checks the position has a stop. The audit's preferred fix also adds a position-level loss cap and a quote-silence watchdog, which need exchange experiments and engine coordination first. What goes in the first implementation batch?

options.label: (a)
options.text: Batch 1 = the five targeted patches now (confirm-before-cancel emergency, rejected-leg branch with alert, reconnect forever with remote paging, side from position sign, restore stop check). The position-level cap and watchdog follow in batch 2 once the exchange experiments answer.

options.label: (b)
options.text: Wait and build everything, including the position-level cap and the watchdog, in one batch after the experiments.

options.label: (c)
options.text: Build only the position-level cap; skip the targeted patches.

items.rationale: (a) ships the guards that cannot make things worse now, before a six-week absence, and leaves the design-dependent cap for when the exchange behaviour is known. (b) delays the S0 fixes for experiments they do not depend on. (c) leaves the false 'Executed' message and the give-up reconnect in place.
